clues: This town is the most big town on the great Arab land tongue that juts in the sea. It lies on the high flat Najd plain, in the east part of that tongue.
This desert city has long, extremely hot summers and short, cold winters. Rain is rare, and dust storms can turn the sky thick.
In 1823, a ruler named Turki chose this oasis town as his new capital. His family, the House of Saud, rules the country to this day.
One skyscraper here splits into two near its top. A sky-bridge joins the two sides, high above the city streets.
The men and women who run Saudi Arabia do their work in this town. It is the chief base of rule for the whole wide land.
